subsystems.name: Entanglement sources
subsystems.role: produce pairs of photons whose quantum states are linked, no matter how far apart they end up.
parts: nonlinear crystals for spontaneous parametric down-conversion

subsystems.name: Quantum memories
subsystems.role: hold a quantum state long enough for the next link to be ready.

subsystems.name: Repeater nodes
subsystems.role: extend range by swapping entanglement from one segment to the next.

subsystems.name: Transmission links
subsystems.role: carry single photons without losing them.

subsystems.name: Classical control plane
subsystems.role: synchronises clocks, routes keys and reports which attempts succeeded.

subsystems.name: End nodes
subsystems.role: the users: quantum key distribution devices today, small quantum processors later.

buildSteps.title: Generate entangled photons
buildSteps.detail: A laser pumps a nonlinear crystal or a quantum dot, which occasionally emits a pair of photons entangled in polarisation or time-bin.

buildSteps.title: Send them down a link
buildSteps.detail: One photon travels through telecom fibre, or through free space to a satellite and back down. Loss rises steeply with distance, so links stay short — tens to a few hundred kilometres at best.

buildSteps.title: Store the state in memory
buildSteps.detail: At the receiving node, the photon's state is mapped into an atomic ensemble or ion, which must keep it coherent for milliseconds or longer.

buildSteps.title: Swap at the middle
buildSteps.detail: Two neighbouring segments each hold half an entangled pair. A joint measurement at the middle node entangles the far ends, stretching the link past the direct-loss limit.

buildSteps.title: Purify and correct
buildSteps.detail: Repeated swapping degrades fidelity, so entanglement distillation and error correction are used to recover a clean link.

buildSteps.title: Chain the segments
buildSteps.detail: Many repeater hops, each with memories, are concatenated until a link spans a continent.

buildSteps.title: Synchronise the network
buildSteps.detail: Ultra-stable clocks and classical signalling tell every node when to measure, so the quantum and classical layers stay in step.

buildSteps.title: Hand off to applications
buildSteps.detail: End nodes use the entanglement for key distribution, clock comparison, or — much further off — to link quantum processors.

prerequisites.tech: Low-loss optical fibre and single-photon detectors
prerequisites.why: every quantum link is built from ordinary telecom hardware plus very sensitive detectors.
routinely made in laboratories, though not yet bright and pure enough for a network.
demonstrated in several systems, but storage times and efficiencies are still far below what a repeater needs.
two- and three-node experiments exist; no repeater chain has operated outside the lab.
entanglement and key distribution have been demonstrated from orbit, but only for short passes and small key volumes.
needed to stop errors accumulating over many hops, and still costly in qubits and hardware.

pathway.milestone: metropolitan quantum key distribution networks using trusted nodes, and satellite-to-ground key distribution demonstrated
pathway.unlocks: point-to-point secret keys over city and country scales, but not end-to-end entanglement.

pathway.milestone: laboratory repeater chains of several memory nodes with entanglement swapping
pathway.unlocks: distance beyond the direct-fibre limit without trusting intermediate nodes.

pathway.milestone: satellite entanglement links combined with ground fibre segments
pathway.unlocks: intercontinental entanglement distribution and a genuinely global key layer.

pathway.milestone: entanglement shared between small quantum processors
pathway.unlocks: distributed quantum computing and networked sensing — note this is not 'instant computation'; entanglement cannot send information faster than light.
